title: The gear computer and its assembled copy

statements.text: A gear computer $\alpha$ runs a 1000-step algorithm said to suffice for consciousness. A second device $\beta$ is assembled directly into $\alpha$'s state at a later step without running it. By state sufficiency the two evolve identically, so a process theory's different attributions to them can never show up in a test.

sources.quote: a process theory can never offer a direct test, even in principle, to show that consciousness depends on prior history, rather than on the current state of the system at the time of the attribution
